# Checkbox group — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a checkbox group when a set of options is one question with several right answers — which notifications to receive, which roles to grant, which columns to show. The group owns the aggregate value, so you get one change event carrying the whole selection instead of tracking each box yourself. Each item takes its label as a required prop, because an unnamed option in a list is worse than a missing one. For a set where only one answer is allowed, use a radio group instead.

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| CheckboxGroupRoot | The group. Owns the aggregate selection and emits one change carrying the whole value. |
| CheckboxGroupItem | One option. Takes `label` as a required prop and renders its own `<label>`, so each item is named by construction. |
| CheckboxGroup | The namespace object: Root and Item. |

## Native

### Features

Reach for a checkbox group when several things can be chosen at once and the result is a set: filters, permissions, options. The group owns the selection — `value` is a `string[]` and every change reports the whole list — so the state is one thing rather than many. `disabled` on the group disables every item unless an item overrides it, which is the same inherited-disabled idea the fieldset family implements for arbitrary controls. Each item names itself from its `children` when they are a plain string, so the common case needs no labelling work.
